blockMcqs.question: Why does caching work at all?
options: Databases are always slower than RAM
Workloads have locality — a hot set repeats
blockMcqs.explanation: A small hot set of keys serves most traffic, so few entries satisfy most reads.

blockMcqs.question: In cache-aside, who handles a cache miss?
options: The cache layer fetches and fills itself
The application reads the DB and populates
The database pushes into the cache
blockMcqs.explanation: Cache-aside puts miss logic in the app; read-through moves it into the cache.

blockMcqs.question: What is the main risk of write-back caching?
options: It can lose data if the node crashes
It floods the database on every write
blockMcqs.explanation: Write-back acknowledges before flushing to the DB, so a crash loses unflushed writes.

blockMcqs.question: Why delete a cache key on write instead of updating it?
options: Updates are not supported by Redis
Deletes are idempotent and avoid update races
blockMcqs.explanation: Concurrent in-place updates can interleave and leave a stale value; a delete forces a clean re-read.

blockMcqs.question: What breaks with `node = hash(key) % N` sharding?
options: Changing N remaps almost every key
blockMcqs.explanation: A membership change shifts N, causing a mass miss; consistent hashing moves only ~1/N keys.

blockMcqs.question: Which fix prevents a cache stampede?
options: A Bloom filter on missing keys
A single-flight lock so one request rebuilds
blockMcqs.explanation: Single-flight lets one request rebuild the expired key while others wait, not all hammering the DB.

blockMcqs.question: When pick Redis over Memcached?
options: You need data structures, persistence, or pub/sub
You want the absolute simplest blob cache
You need to scale reads across CPU cores
blockMcqs.explanation: Redis adds structures, persistence, and clustering; Memcached is the minimal multi-threaded choice.

blockMcqs.question: Hit ratio drops from 90% to 80%. What happens to DB load?
blockMcqs.explanation: DB load tracks misses; 10% to 20% misses doubles the requests reaching the database.
